451: Great people are afraid of mixing with mean, small-minded people. But small-minded people pull such people close and treat them like their own family.
452: Water changes its color and taste depending on the ground it flows over. In the same way, a person’s understanding takes on the nature of the people they spend time with.
453: Our power to understand things comes from our own mind. But how others judge us, saying “that is the kind of person they are,” comes from the friends we keep.
454: A person’s good sense seems to live in their own mind. But it really comes from the group of people they spend time with.
455: A clean, pure mind and clean, pure actions both come from keeping company with good, pure people.
456: People with pure minds leave behind a good name for those who come after them. People who keep pure company never do anything that is not good.
457: A good mind brings a person success and plenty. Good friends bring them every kind of praise and fame.
458: Even wise people who already have a very good mind find that good friends make them safer and stronger.
459: A good mind earns a happy life in the next world. Even that is made safe by keeping good company.
460: Nothing helps a person more than good friends, and nothing causes more pain and trouble than bad friends.
461: Before you do something, think about what you will lose, what you will gain, and what good will be left in the end. Only then begin.
462: Nothing is too hard for people who first talk things over with carefully chosen advisers and then study the matter themselves before they act.
463: Wise people will not take on a project that risks losing the money they already have just in the hope of making more later.
464: People who are afraid of being shamed by failure will not start anything whose plan and outcome are not clear to them.
465: If you rise up to fight enemies without planning every step, you are like a farmer preparing a field for them, where they will grow strong.
466: Doing what you should not do ruins you. Not doing what you should do ruins you just as much.
467: Think it through first, and then decide what to do. Saying “we will think about it after we start” is shameful.
468: Work that is not done the right way will fail, even if many people stand by to help and protect it.
469: Even when you try to do good, you can fail if you do not understand what each person is like and what suits them.
470: Think carefully and do only things the world will not look down on. People do not accept actions that do not fit who you are and your place in life.
471: Before you act, compare four strengths: how much strength the job needs, how strong you are, how strong your opponent is, and how strong the helpers on each side are.
472: Nothing is out of reach for people who know what they can do, learn what the job needs, and keep working steadily at it.
473: Many people did not know how strong they really were. They rushed into a task on excitement alone and broke down halfway.
474: A person who does not get along with others, does not know their own limits, and thinks too highly of themselves will soon be ruined.
475: Even peacock feathers, which are very light, will break the axle of a cart if you pile on too many.
476: A person who has climbed to the very tip of a tree branch and tries to climb even higher will fall and lose their life.
477: Know how much you have, and give in a sensible way. That is how you keep your money safe while still giving.
478: It does no harm if the money coming in is small, as long as the money going out is not bigger.
479: A person who does not live within what they can afford may seem to be doing well, but their life will vanish and leave nothing behind.
480: Giving away money without thinking about how much you really have will soon use up everything you own.
481: In the daytime even a crow can beat the stronger owl. In the same way, a king who wants to beat his enemies must wait for the right time.
482: Acting at the right time is like a rope that ties good fortune down so it cannot slip away from you.
483: Is any task truly impossible if you do it with the right tools and at the right time?
484: Even if you aim to win the whole world, you can get it, as long as you choose the right time and the right place to act.
485: People who want to win the world do not get upset or hasty. They wait calmly and watch for the right time.
486: When a strong, active person holds back for a while, it is like a fighting ram stepping back so it can charge harder.
487: Wise people do not burst out in anger right away. They keep it inside and wait for the right time to act.
488: When you meet your enemies, put up with them and even show them respect. When their time to fall comes, they will fall headfirst.
489: When a rare chance comes, grab it at once and do the thing that would be too hard to do at any other time.
490: When the time is not right, wait quietly like a heron standing still. When the right moment comes, strike as fast and sure as the heron catches a fish.
491: Do not start a fight against an enemy, and do not look down on them, until you have found a place from which you can surround and defeat them.
492: Even for people who are already strong in battle, fighting from a safe, well-protected place gives them many extra advantages.
493: Even weak people can become strong enough to win if they pick the right place, protect themselves well, and then act against their enemy.
494: If people who have found the right place stay close to it and act from there, the enemies who planned to beat them will have to give up.
495: In deep water a crocodile can beat other animals. But once it leaves the water, those same animals can beat it.
496: A tall chariot with strong wheels cannot run on the sea, and a ship that sails the sea cannot run on land.
497: If you think everything through carefully and act from the right place, you need no other helper except your own courage.
498: If a leader with a small army stands on ground where it can fight well, a leader with a big army will lose his push and his advantage.
499: Even people with no strong fort and no great power are hard to beat if you attack them in their own homeland.
500: A brave war elephant that can pierce spear-carrying soldiers with its tusks can be killed even by jackals when it gets stuck in deep mud.
501: Give a person an important job only after testing them in four ways: with doing right, with money, with pleasure, and with fear for their own life.
502: Trust a person who comes from a good family, has no faults, and is so afraid of shame that they guard their good name.
503: Even among people who have studied hard books and seem to have no faults, if you look closely, it is rare to find one with no ignorance at all.
504: Look at a person’s good points, then at their faults. See which side is bigger, and judge them by that.
505: Whether a person is great or mean and small, their own actions are the test that shows it.
506: Do not trust people who have no family or community ties. With no one to answer to, they feel no shame about doing wrong.
507: Trusting people who do not have the knowledge they need, just because you like them, will lead to every kind of foolish mistake.
508: Someone who trusts a stranger without checking them first brings endless trouble, even to their own children and grandchildren.
509: Do not trust anyone without checking them first. After checking, trust them with the things they can be trusted with.
510: Trusting someone you have not checked, and doubting someone you checked and then trusted, both bring endless trouble.
511: Give the job to the person who weighs the good and the bad in a matter and then naturally chooses to do what is good.
512: Give the work to someone who can find more ways to bring money in, make it grow, and spot and fix the problems that come up.
513: You can safely trust a person who fully has these four things: loyal love, knowledge, clear and firm thinking, and freedom from greed.
514: Even after being tested and approved in every way, many people turn out to be different once they actually start doing the work.
515: Give a job only to someone who knows how to do it and can push through the hard parts to finish it. Never give it to someone just because you like or admire them.
516: First judge the person who will do the work, then judge the work itself, and then act when the time is right for both.
517: Once you decide that “this person can do this job in this way,” hand the job over to them and leave it in their hands.
518: After finding out what work a person is good at, put them fully in charge of it and give them the power to do it.
519: Good fortune leaves a ruler who misjudges and becomes suspicious of a worker’s closeness when that worker is truly devoted to the job.
520: A king should check every day how his workers behave. As long as they do not go wrong, the country will not go wrong either.
521: Even when a man has lost everything he had, only his relatives still honor the old bond they shared with him.
522: If a man has relatives whose love never fails, they will bring him many kinds of good fortune that keep on growing.
523: A man who does not share his heart with his relatives is like a big pond with no banks: whatever water comes in just flows away.
524: The real reward of becoming rich is living in a way that keeps your relatives gathered around you.
525: A man who gives freely and speaks kindly will be surrounded by relatives, circle after circle of them.
526: No one on this wide earth has more relatives around him than a man who gives generously and does not hold on to anger.
527: A crow does not hide its food. It calls its family with a caw and eats with them. Good fortune comes only to people who are like that.
528: If a king does not treat everyone the same but gives each person the respect their worth deserves, many people will stay close to him because of it.
529: Relatives who were once close but left because of some hurt will come back on their own once the cause of the fight is gone.
530: When a relative who left the king for no reason comes back wanting something, the king should give what they need, but wait and judge them carefully before taking them back.
531: Becoming careless because you are carried away by great joy does more harm than even anger that has gone out of control.
532: Just as being poor day after day slowly destroys a person’s mind, being careless and forgetful destroys a person’s good name.
533: Careless, forgetful people never win lasting fame. The writers of every kind of book in the world agree on this.
534: A fort is no use to someone who is a coward at heart. In the same way, no advantage is any use to someone who is careless.
535: Someone who carelessly fails to guard against trouble before it comes will be sorry for their own mistake when the trouble hits.
536: If a person can stay alert and careful toward everyone and at all times, nothing else is as good as that.
537: No job is too hard, however difficult people say it is, if you do it carefully, with a mind that never forgets or slips.
538: Do carefully the things that wise people have praised. Those who ignore them and leave them undone will find no good in any of their seven births (the many lives a person is believed to live).
539: Whenever you feel full of pride and pleased with yourself, remember the people who were ruined because they got careless.
540: It is easy to reach your goal, as long as you keep your mind fixed on it from then on.
541: Justice means looking into every case carefully, not favoring anyone, being fair, and acting only after talking it over with people who know the law.
542: All living things on earth look up to the sky for rain. In the same way, the people of a country look to their king’s fair rule in order to live.
543: A king’s fair rule is what holds up the holy books of the learned priests and the dharma (the right way of living) that those books teach.
544: The whole world holds on to the feet of a great king who rules with love and keeps his people close.
545: In the country of a king who rules by fair law, the seasonal rains come and the harvests are rich, both together.
546: A king wins not by his spear but by his scepter (his rule), as long as that rule stays straight and fair.
547: The king protects the whole world, and justice protects the king, as long as he never fails to do justice.
548: A king whom people cannot easily reach, and who does not look into their problems and give fair judgments, will fall low and be ruined, even without an enemy.
549: Protecting the people from outside harm, caring for them, and punishing crime is not a fault in a king. It is his proper job.
550: When a king punishes cruel killers with death, it is like a farmer pulling out weeds to protect the young crop.
551: A king who keeps hurting his people and keeps doing unjust things is crueler than a person who kills for a living.
552: When a king demands money from his people, it is like a robber with a spear standing on a lonely road and saying, “Give it to me.”
553: A king who does not look into wrongs every day and give fair judgments will watch his country grow weaker every day.
554: A king who twists justice and acts without thinking about what will happen will lose both his riches and his people at once.
555: The tears of people who are suffering more than they can bear are a weapon that wears away a cruel king’s riches.
556: Fair rule is what makes a king’s fame last. Without it, his glory will not stay.
557: A king without kindness is to his people what a lack of rain is to the earth.
558: Under an unfair king, having money brings more misery than having nothing at all.
559: If a king rules unfairly, the seasons go wrong and the clouds will not give rain.
560: If the ruler does not protect the land, the cows give less milk and the learned priests who do the six sacred duties forget their holy books.
561: A true king looks into a wrong fairly and carefully, then punishes it in a way that fits the crime, so that it does not happen again.
562: Rulers who want their good times to last should raise the stick sternly but bring it down gently. They should warn firmly but punish mildly.
563: A cruel king who keeps doing things that fill his people with fear will surely and quickly be ruined.
564: A king whose people call him “our cruel ruler” will have his life cut short and will quickly be destroyed.
565: The great riches of a ruler who is hard to meet and who greets people with an angry face are like treasure guarded by a demon. They are scary and help no one.
566: If a ruler speaks harshly and shows no kindness, his great riches will not last. They will disappear right then.
567: Harsh words and punishments that go too far are like a file that slowly wears down a king’s power to beat his enemies.
568: A king who does not think things through with his advisers, and then gets angry and blames them, will see his good fortune shrink.
569: A king who has not built a safe place of defense ahead of time will be filled with fear when war comes, and will quickly be destroyed.
570: A cruel ruler who keeps ignorant, unlearned people as his helpers is the heaviest weight the earth has to carry. There is none heavier.
571: The world keeps going only because of a very great beauty called kannottam (looking at others with kindness and care).
572: All the everyday business of the world runs on kindness toward others. People without it are just a burden on the earth.
573: What use is a tune that does not fit the song? In the same way, what use is an eye that shows no kindness?
574: Eyes that show no proper kindness only seem to be there in the face. What else are they good for?
575: Kindness is the jewel that makes the eye beautiful. Without it, the eyes will look like nothing more than two sores.
576: People who have eyes but never look kindly at others are like trees standing in the ground. They have the shape but not the feeling.
577: People without kindness are really without eyes. And people who truly have eyes are never without kindness.
578: The world truly belongs to those who can show kindness without letting their duty be harmed.
579: The highest goodness is to show kindness and patiently put up with even those who like to hurt us.
580: People who want the kind of politeness everyone admires will even drink poison they watched a friend pour for them, and still stay friends.
581: A ruler should know that he has two eyes: his spies, who show him what is really happening, and the respected books of law, which show him what should be done.
582: A king’s job is to find out quickly, at all times, everything that happens to everyone, whether they are enemies, friends, or neither.
583: A king who does not collect news through spies and understand what it means has no way to win.
584: A true spy watches everyone without exception: the king’s own officers, his relatives, and his enemies too.
585: A real spy looks ordinary so no one suspects him, does not get nervous when people stare, and never lets his secret slip anywhere.
586: A spy dresses up as a holy man who has given up the world, gets into places others cannot enter, finds out everything, and never gives himself away, whatever is done to him.
587: A spy is someone who can uncover hidden secrets and has no doubt at all about what he has found.
588: Even news that a spy has brought in should be believed only after another spy has checked it.
589: Use spies so that none of them knows about the others. When three such spies report the same thing, you can believe it.
590: A king should not reward a spy where others can see. If he does, he gives away his own secret.
591: Only inner drive truly makes a person rich. People without it do not really own anything, whatever else they have.
592: A strong, eager mind is the thing you own that lasts. Money and things do not stay. They slip away.
593: People who keep a firm hold on their inner drive do not cry, “We have lost our money.”
594: Good fortune itself asks for directions and goes to the home of a person whose drive never weakens.
595: The stem of a water lily grows as tall as the water is deep. In the same way, a person rises only as high as the drive in their mind.
596: Always think about rising higher. Even if bad luck keeps you from reaching your goal, aiming high still has the worth of a goal that did not fail.
597: Strong-minded people do not give up even when they are ruined, just as a war elephant stands firm with pride even when arrows are stuck deep in its body.
598: People without inner drive will never know the proud joy of saying, “We are the generous givers of the world.”
599: An elephant is huge and has sharp tusks, yet it gets scared when a tiger attacks.
600: A person’s real strength is having lots of inner drive. People without it are just trees that happen to have human shape.
